::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jany 1st 1868  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA; Collection 846 (Mulock Family Papers), Box 2, Folder 14
:::

Dear [Mrs. Craik](people/person_378.qmd),
Your note and enclosure have followed me to the home where I am staying a few days (in spite of the address on my paper). Many thanks for it.

I read with much interest the account of the [Little Sisters](organizations/other_197.qmd) in the Magazine.[^1] It is curious how they make their way with all kinds of people, even at Plymouth, the last place where I should have expected them to thrive.[^2]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: 'Good Catholics, being the history of \\"Les Petites Soeurs des Pauvres\\"' by Henriette de Witt appeared in the January 1868 issue of *[Macmillan's Magazine](organizations/other_78.qmd)*.
[^2]: No doubt because of Plymouth's strong Nonconformist tradition and the opposition which had met Lydia Sellon’s attempts to establish a sisterhood there.
